description: Original TOEFL-style Take an Interview questions for vocabulary transfer. Difficulty tags are editorial estimates, not empirically calibrated.

questions.prompt: How can digital resources help students study independently? Give an example.
questions.example_html: Digital libraries <mark>enable</mark> students to research topics without visiting campus.
questions.instruction: In your answer, use ENABLE to explain what makes independent learning possible.

questions.prompt: Tell me about an experience that gave you more confidence to make decisions about your learning.
questions.example_html: A successful independent project can <mark>empower</mark> students to make their own academic decisions.
questions.instruction: Use EMPOWER to describe how a learning experience can give someone more confidence or control.

questions.prompt: Some students rarely participate in class. What could a teacher do to change that?
questions.example_html: Asking open questions can <mark>encourage</mark> quieter students to share their ideas.
questions.instruction: Use ENCOURAGE to suggest a way teachers could motivate students.

questions.prompt: Do you think giving students more freedom to choose classes would improve their learning? Why?
questions.example_html: Flexible course options <mark>enable</mark> students to pursue subjects that match their goals.
questions.instruction: Use ENABLE to explain a benefit of giving students more control over their education.

questions.prompt: What is one activity outside regular classes that could help students understand other cultures?
questions.example_html: Cultural exchange programs <mark>enrich</mark> students' understanding of other societies.
questions.instruction: Use ENRICH to explain how an extracurricular activity can add value to someone's experience.

questions.prompt: Have you ever taken part in an activity that improved a useful skill? What did it help you do?
questions.example_html: Debate clubs can <mark>enhance</mark> students' public-speaking skills.
questions.instruction: Use ENHANCE to explain how an activity improves a particular skill.

questions.prompt: Suppose your university library is too small. What would you suggest changing, and why?
questions.example_html: The university could <mark>enlarge</mark> the library's study area to accommodate more students.
questions.instruction: Use ENLARGE to recommend increasing the physical size of something or expanding a collection.

questions.prompt: Should universities provide cultural activities as well as academic courses? Why or why not?
questions.example_html: Exposure to art and history can <mark>enrich</mark> students' perspectives.
questions.instruction: Use ENRICH when explaining why education should include more than academic knowledge.

questions.prompt: What is one school rule you consider important, and how should schools make sure students follow it?
questions.example_html: Schools should <mark>enforce</mark> anti-bullying policies consistently.
questions.instruction: Use ENFORCE to describe how an institution makes people follow a rule.

questions.prompt: Why do students sometimes ignore school rules, and what could administrators do about it?
questions.example_html: When administrators fail to <mark>enforce</mark> rules consistently, students may stop taking them seriously.
questions.instruction: Use ENFORCE to explain why some rules are not followed.

questions.prompt: Imagine that a university wants to introduce a formal regulation about noise in study areas. What should it include?
questions.example_html: The university could <mark>enact</mark> a regulation restricting loud phone calls in libraries.
questions.instruction: Use ENACT to explain the introduction of a formal new regulation. Do not confuse enacting a rule with enforcing it.

questions.prompt: Should students have a formal right to participate in decisions about university policies? Explain your view.
questions.example_html: Students should be <mark>entitled</mark> to express concerns about policies that affect them.
questions.instruction: Use BE ENTITLED TO to explain a right that students should have.

questions.prompt: What digital feature would you add directly to an online course to help students stay organized?
questions.example_html: Teachers could <mark>embed</mark> reminders into the course platform.
questions.instruction: Use EMBED to describe incorporating a feature or resource into something larger.

questions.prompt: When a lecture covers a complicated topic, how do you summarize its most important point?
questions.example_html: A well-designed diagram can <mark>encapsulate</mark> the main idea of a lecture.
questions.instruction: Use ENCAPSULATE to explain how a short summary communicates a complex idea.

questions.prompt: Imagine you're designing a learning platform. Which features would you integrate directly into lessons?
questions.example_html: Developers could <mark>embed</mark> short quizzes into every lesson.
questions.instruction: Use EMBED to recommend an interactive feature inside a learning platform.

questions.prompt: Universities collect information from many departments. Why might it be useful to store that information in a consistent digital format?
questions.example_html: Universities can <mark>encode</mark> records in a standard format to make them easier to process.
questions.instruction: Use ENCODE to describe converting information into a standardized digital form, not keeping it secret.
questions.pattern: encode + data / information + in / as + a format

questions.prompt: What qualities should a welcoming university demonstrate through its everyday practices?
questions.example_html: A truly inclusive university should <mark>embody</mark> respect for different backgrounds.
questions.instruction: Use EMBODY to explain how an institution demonstrates a value through its actions.

questions.prompt: Can you describe someone whose actions show a quality you particularly admire?
questions.example_html: A mentor who treats everyone fairly can <mark>embody</mark> integrity.
questions.instruction: Use EMBODY to describe a person who represents an important value.

questions.prompt: If a university creates a student well-being program, which parts of student life should it address?
questions.example_html: The program should <mark>encompass</mark> academic guidance, mental well-being and financial support.
questions.instruction: Use ENCOMPASS to explain the range of needs a student-support program should cover.
questions.pattern: encompass + several areas / a range of needs

questions.prompt: How much responsibility should a university take for giving students equal opportunities to succeed?
questions.example_html: Universities should <mark>ensure</mark> that essential learning materials are accessible to all students.
questions.instruction: Use ENSURE to explain how a university can make an outcome more likely or certain.

questions.prompt: Why is it important for universities to protect natural spaces on campus?
questions.example_html: Removing green areas could <mark>endanger</mark> local wildlife.
questions.instruction: Use ENDANGER to explain a risk to wildlife, health or safety.
questions.pattern: endanger + wildlife / public safety / an ecosystem

questions.prompt: When might it be reasonable for a school to put a fence around part of its outdoor space?
questions.example_html: A university might <mark>enclose</mark> a garden to protect newly planted trees.
questions.instruction: Use ENCLOSE to describe placing a physical boundary around a space.
questions.pattern: enclose + a space + with a fence / wall

questions.prompt: Imagine a new campus building would replace part of a garden. What environmental consequences should officials consider?
questions.example_html: Construction could <mark>endanger</mark> local biodiversity unless protective measures are taken.
questions.instruction: Use ENDANGER when explaining a potential environmental risk of a construction project.

questions.prompt: Why can long-established institutional practices be difficult to change, even when they cause problems?
questions.example_html: Repeatedly following outdated procedures can <mark>entrench</mark> inefficient practices.
questions.instruction: Use ENTRENCH to explain how a problem becomes difficult to change over time.
